title: microtide-slippage-latency-cost-field-notes
body:
Microtide slippage = small, repeated session shifts that cause p95/p99 to drift up over ~10-60s windows.

Objective:
- Capture an easy-to-reproduce microtide scenario and show latency vs $/1k-token tradeoffs across three serving configs.
- Produce a compact ASCII-style visualization suitable for inclusion in a one-slide collateral.

Summary (quick take):
- Quantized-multiplex reduces nominal cost by ~46% vs baseline but introduces a 1.2–1.8x p99 inflation under microtide conditions.
- Edge-instance (small GPU) looks cheaper at low sustained QPS but is fragile to microtide slippage (p99 spikes).
- Heuristic: prefer quantized-multiplex for stable session pools; prefer baseline-fastpath for interactive edges where tight p99 matters.

Bench setup (notes, informal):
- Model: redwood-open-13B (fp16 / int8-quant profile used)
- Inputs: mixed-session mix: 40% short prompts (≤32 tokens), 50% medium (32–128), 10% long (>=512)
- Client: 50 synthetic clients generating poisson arrivals with 10s mean session interarrival -> produces microtide pattern (bursts every ~12–18s)
- Duration: 30m per config; repeated 3 runs, median presented here.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 for latency (ms), throughput (qps), estimated $/1k tokens (units use internal token-cost model: infra+GPU amortization + service overhead)

Configs tested:
A) baseline-core: dedicated fast-path, fp16, pinned model shards
B) quantized-multiplex: int8 quant, continuous multiplexing slots (higher packing), prefix caching enabled
C) edge-small: single small GPU, lower memory headroom, opportunistic prefetch off

Compact results table (median across runs):

Config | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | QPS | $ / 1k tokens
-------|---------|---------|---------|-----|------------
baseline-core   | 85   | 160  | 420 | 210 | $0.048
quantized-multiplex | 95   | 180  | 610 | 260 | $0.026
edge-small      | 110  | 240  | 980 | 75  | $0.037

Notes on numbers:
- baseline-core gives lower p99 because of fastpath preemption and dedicated shards; throughput is modest vs multiplex but p99 is stable.
- quantized-multiplex increases throughput (more packing) and cuts token cost ~46% vs baseline but p99 shows occasional wide tails in the microtide windows.
- edge-small has poor tail behavior; p99 sometimes exceeds 1s due to memory pressure and GC-like stalls we suspect in local allocator.

ASCII microtide p99 trace (30s window sample, normalized ms values, one char ~25ms):
Time -> 0s                            15s                             30s
baseline-core    : ||||||||||||||||||||-----|||||||||||||||||----|||||     (p99: 420ms steady-ish)
quantized-multiplex: ||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||    (p99: climbs to 610ms during tides)
edge-small       : |||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||| (p99: spikes to ~980ms, frequent)
interpretation:
- Tradeoff surface: cost vs tail. quantized-multiplex wins on token unit cost but loses on tail under microtide patterns.
- Microtide slippage mechanism hypothesis: multiplex packing reorders session slots and when a sequence of medium-length sessions overlap, KV cache churn leads to cache misses + more kernel transitions, driving p99 up.
- Edge instability likely allocator / memcpy pressure + opportunistic prefetch off.
- If customer SLA is p99 < 500ms, baseline-core or canary fastpath should be default; for cost-conscious workloads with relaxed p99, quantized-multiplex is strong.
open_questions:
- Can we mitigate multiplex tail by smarter admission control (max slot age?) or by soft-evicting cold KV items?
- Does int8 path amplify kernel-switch overheads? Need microprofiling.
- How correlated are microtide spikes with prompt length distribution skew in live traffic?
next_steps:
1) Run microprofiling (tracewalk) under quantized-multiplex with per-kernel timing (todo: JIRA-ENG-7421).
2) Test a variant: multiplex + min-slot-reserve (hold 10% of GPU lanes warm for 1s sessions) -> see if p99 improves.
3) Add a small-note artifact: one-slide ASCII graphic + 3 bullet recommendation for product collateral.
4) Draft short user-facing blurb for Optimize: when to pick quantized-multiplex vs baseline-fastpath.
